spans.s:
ययाति ययाति, m., N. of a celebrated
monarch of the lunar race (son of king Nahuṣa,
whom he succeeded; he first married the daughter
of Uśanas or Śukra, Devayānī, who had been thrown
into a well by Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣa-parvan;
Yayāti having found her and wedded her, she de-
manded that Śarmiṣṭhā, who had ill-treated her,
should become her handmaid; this was granted, but
Yayāti then fell in love with the handmaid and
secretly married her, for which the father of Deva-
yānī inflicted on him premature decay; from the
two wives of Yayāti came the two lines of the lunar
race, Yadu being the son of Devayānī, and Puru of
Śarmiṣṭhā; Yayāti Nāhuṣa is represented as the
author of Ṛg-veda

-6).
—ययाति-चरित,
अम्, n. the history of Yayāti; N. of a drama in seven
acts by Rudra-deva (celebrating the amours of Yayāti
and Śarmiṣṭhā).
—ययाति-पतन, अम्, n. ‘fall of
Yayāti,’ N. of a place of pilgrimage.
—ययाति-
विजय, अस्, m. ‘Yayāti's victory,’ N. of a work.
ययावर ययावर for यायावर, q. v.

यायावर, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens.), going
repeatedly; wandering in all directions, having no
fixed or permanent abode; (अस्), m. a vagrant men-
dicant, saint; a horse selected for the horse sacrifice
(‘wandering at large’); a Brāhman who has pre-
served his household fire (?); N. of Jarat-kāru;
(आस्), m. pl., N. of a family of Brāhmans (to which
Jarat-kāru belonged); (अम्), n. the life of a wan-
dering beggar.

यायावर यायावर, यायिन्. See p. 814,
col. 2.

ययि ययि, इस्, इस्, इ, or ययी, ईस्, ईस्, इ (fr. rt.
1. या), Ved. going, moving, hastening, swift, quick;
(ईस्), m. a horse; a road; Śiva; a cloud, (in this
sense the gender is doubtful.)
ययिन्, ई, m., N. of Śiva.

यायिन्, ई, इनी, इ, going, moving, travelling, jour-
neying, marching, running, riding, driving, flying;
a traveller, passenger; riding or going in or on,
(generally at the end of comps., e. g. गज-यायिन्,
riding on an elephant; cf. नौ-य्˚); going to, jour-
neying towards; going on an expedition, taking the
field, going to war; opposing each other (said of
planets; cf. ग्रह-युद्ध).
ययिवस्, वान्, युषी, वत्, who or what has gone.

ययु, उस्, उस्, उ, going, moving, hastening, quick,
swift; (उस्), m. a horse fit for sacrifice (‘one running
about wild’); a horse (generally).

यायजूक यायजूक, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Intens.
of rt. 1. यज्), frequently sacrificing, constantly mak-
ing offerings, devout; (अस्), m. a performer of fre-
quent sacrifices.

यायात यायात, अस्, ई, अम्, relating to Ya-
yāti, belonging to Yayāti, &c.; (अम्), n., N. of the
eighteenth chapter of the ninth book of the Bhāga-
vata-Purāṇa (containing an account of Yayāti).
